metaDescription: Odoo HR implementation detail: employee master data, contracts, org chart, onboarding plans, what Community includes, and the GCC and EU compliance catch.
intro: Odoo HR is the record every other HR app reads. Time Off checks the working schedule on the employee, Attendance matches a badge to it, Timesheets cost hours against it, Payroll reads the contract attached to it, and Expenses raise a liability against the person behind it. Nothing else in the suite behaves until that record is right, which is why an HR rollout is mostly a data exercise and only partly a configuration one.

The app is Community. Employees, departments, job positions, the org chart, skills, resume lines, contracts and the departure workflow ship at no licence cost, as do Time Off, Attendance, Timesheets and Recruitment. Payroll, Appraisals, Documents, Sign, Approvals and Planning are Enterprise. That line matters because the features buyers picture when they say HRMS sit on both sides of it, and the edition question is settled by whether a payslip has to come out of Odoo rather than by the size of the directory.

Odoo also separates the employee from the user. Somebody can exist as an employee, be paid, book leave and appear on the org chart without ever logging in, and that person costs nothing in licence terms. Only people who work in the backend consume a user. Getting that split wrong is the fastest way to quote a project at several times its real subscription cost.
whoFor: Companies of fifty staff and up who keep the employee list in a spreadsheet and find during an audit that three copies of it disagree.
Groups running several legal entities in one database that want one directory, one org chart and per company access rules.
GCC employers tracking iqama, Emirates ID, QID, labour card and passport expiry against a real person rather than a folder on a shared drive.
Service businesses whose cost, capacity and utilisation reporting depends on the employee record being accurate.
It is not a standalone HRMS purchase, because the two things most buyers ask for first, payslips and appraisals, are separate Enterprise apps.
It is a weak fit where confidentiality has to work field by field inside HR, since Odoo restricts personal data to the HR Officer group as one block.

capabilities.title: The employee record, stored twice
capabilities.body: Odoo keeps each person in two forms. The full record holds identification numbers, private address, bank account, marital status, dependants and visa data, and only the HR Officer and HR Administrator groups can read it. A public version carries work email, phone, department, manager and job title, and that is what a colleague sees in the directory or on a task. The split explains why the list looks empty of personal data to most users, and why an import has to run as an HR user.

capabilities.title: Departments, jobs and the manager tree
capabilities.body: Departments carry a parent department and a manager, so the structure is a tree rather than a flat list. Job positions are separate records holding expected headcount, which is what Recruitment opens a vacancy against. The manager field on the employee draws the org chart and, more importantly, routes approvals in Time Off, Timesheets and Expenses. An employee with no manager is not a cosmetic gap, it is a request that reaches nobody.

capabilities.title: Contracts, wage and salary structure
capabilities.body: A contract holds the start and end date, the wage, the working schedule and the salary structure type, and it is the contract rather than the employee that payroll reads. Contracts are dated, so a raise is a new contract and the history stays intact. A scheduled job moves a contract to expired once its end date passes and raises an activity for the responsible user, which is how fixed term populations in the Gulf get warning instead of a surprise.

capabilities.title: Skills, resume lines and certifications
capabilities.body: The skills tab records a skill, its type and a level on a scale you define, so language, technical and behavioural skills can each be scored differently. The resume section holds experience, education and certification lines with dates, which is where professional licences and training certificates live. Expiry is not an alert by itself, so most projects add a computed next expiry date and one filtered list so renewals surface before they lapse.

capabilities.title: Onboarding and offboarding as activity plans
capabilities.body: Odoo builds checklists as scheduled activities rather than as a task list. You define a plan once, listing each step and the role it belongs to, then launch it from the employee record and every step lands as a dated activity in the right person inbox. Offboarding runs the same way, ending in a departure wizard that records the reason and date and archives the employee instead of deleting them, so payslips, timesheets and attendance history stay readable.

capabilities.title: Documents, identity data and expiry
capabilities.body: Every employee record has a chatter, so contracts, ID scans and signed policies can be attached with no extra licence. That is storage, not document management. Retention rules, folder level access, tagging and asking an employee to upload a missing file come from the Documents app, which is Enterprise. Visa number, work permit number and their expiry dates are native fields on the employee, and a Gulf compliance report is built from those.

capabilities.title: Headcount and cost reporting
capabilities.body: The employee list is an ordinary Odoo model, so headcount by department, by job, by nationality or by contract end date is a filter and a grouping rather than a report to build. Hourly cost sits on the employee and feeds timesheet cost and project margin. Anything needing point in time headcount, joiners and leavers, or turnover percentage depends on the departure date being populated, which is the real reason the departure wizard matters.

setup.title: Working schedules before anything else
setup.body: The working schedule on an employee is a resource calendar, and it decides how a leave request converts into days, when attendance becomes overtime and what capacity Planning assumes. The shipped default is forty hours, Monday to Friday. In Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Kuwait the week runs Sunday to Thursday, and Ramadan hours are a separate calendar again. Build the calendars first, because changing one later does not recalculate allocations already granted.

setup.title: Splitting basic pay from allowances
setup.body: The contract carries one wage figure. Across the Gulf, end of service is calculated on basic salary only, and housing, transport, medical and other allowances are excluded. Qatar goes further and defines the statutory minimum as components rather than a total. So the contract needs a field per component and salary rules that read them, which is Enterprise payroll configuration or a small custom module. Decide it before importing contracts rather than reimporting all of them later.

setup.title: Access rights, and what a line manager sees
setup.body: There are two HR groups. Officer reads and edits personal data, Administrator adds configuration on top. Odoo gives no field level restriction inside that, so an Officer who can see a passport number can also see a salary. Limiting an Officer to one department or one company is a record rule written during implementation, not a checkbox. A line manager in no HR group sees the public record plus the requests of people reporting to them.

setup.title: Importing the existing employee list
setup.body: Import in two passes. The first creates every employee with no manager, the second sets the manager, because that field points at a record which may not exist yet on the first pass. Keep the legacy employee number in the file and map it to the badge ID or a reference field, since attendance hardware, bank files and every old report still speak that number. Run the import as an HR user or the personal fields are refused.

setup.title: Service dates and opening leave balances
setup.body: Two figures never arrive on their own. Length of service for gratuity runs from the original joining date, which is usually earlier than the first contract created in Odoo, so a historical contract or a dedicated field has to carry it. Opening leave balances are not a number typed on the employee, they are allocation records, so each person needs one allocation per leave type with the carried forward figure and a clear cut off date.

setup.title: Wiring onboarding to the apps that do the work
setup.body: An onboarding plan is only a set of activities. The value is in what each step triggers: a laptop issued from Maintenance, a vehicle assigned in Fleet, an offer letter sent through Sign, a request cleared in Approvals, a first payslip in Payroll. Three of those five are Enterprise. Map the steps against the apps you are actually licensing before promising the HR team a one click starter pack.

pitfalls.title: Counting employees as users
pitfalls.body: Odoo bills internal users, not headcount. A plant with four hundred staff and twelve people who work in the backend is twelve users. Someone who only badges in at a shared kiosk, appears on a roster or is paid in a batch never needs a login at all. Budgets get inflated by a factor of ten because the employee list and the user list were treated as the same thing, and the correction is a licensing conversation rather than a technical one.

pitfalls.title: Deleting leavers instead of archiving them
pitfalls.body: An employee who has appeared on a payslip, a timesheet, an attendance line or an expense report cannot be deleted cleanly, and forcing it takes the history with them. Odoo is built around archiving: the departure wizard sets a reason and a date, drops the person out of active lists and keeps every linked record readable. Leavers deleted in year one are the reason turnover and headcount reporting cannot be produced in year two.

pitfalls.title: One working calendar for the whole company
pitfalls.body: Shift crews, part timers, a Ramadan schedule and a head office team do not share a working schedule, yet most first configurations give everyone the default. It surfaces later as leave deducted in the wrong quantity, overtime that never appears and a capacity plan that is confidently wrong. Allocations already issued are not recalculated when the calendar changes, so the correction becomes a data fix stacked on top of a configuration fix.

pitfalls.title: Treating the chatter as a document vault
pitfalls.body: Attachments on an employee record have no expiry, no folder permissions, no retention period and no way to request the missing item from the employee. For passport scans under the GDPR, the Saudi personal data protection law or Turkish KVKK, that is a compliance gap rather than an inconvenience. Either license Documents, or limit what gets attached and keep identity scans in a system that can evidence who opened them.

pitfalls.title: Assuming a localisation exists for your country
pitfalls.body: The HR app is country agnostic. The country specific content, gratuity rules, statutory contributions and payslip layouts, lives in the payroll localisation, and Odoo ships official ones for roughly a dozen countries. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, India, Jordan, Turkiye, Australia and the United States are covered. Pakistan, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Bangladesh, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Canada are not, so those rules are a build or a bought module.

pitfalls.title: Nobody owns the org chart
pitfalls.body: The manager field gets filled once at go live and then decays. Approvals route to someone who left, leave requests sit unanswered because the approver is archived, and the chart shows a department reporting to itself. Make the manager field part of the transfer and departure process rather than a one time import column, and run a monthly list of employees whose manager is no longer active.

worksWith: Time Off, which reads the working schedule and the manager from the employee record to compute balances and route approvals.
Attendance, including ZKTeco and similar biometric readers, matched to the badge ID held on the employee.
Payroll, Enterprise only, which reads the contract rather than the employee for wage, schedule and salary structure.
Recruitment, which converts a hired applicant into an employee and carries the application history across.
Timesheets and Project, where the hourly cost on the employee drives project margin and utilisation.
Expenses, which pays a claim to the employee bank account or reimburses it through a payslip.
Fleet and Maintenance, for the vehicle and the equipment issued to a person on their first day.
LDAP or OAuth single sign on, so the minority who do log in use the corporate directory rather than a second password.

regional.note: Employment contracts are authenticated in Qiwa, so what Odoo holds has to agree with what the ministry holds, job title and wage included. Iqama and passport expiry belong on the employee with a renewal activity, and Nitaqat banding depends on nationality and job data being correct. The Saudi payroll localisation covers GOSI by nationality and end of service, but the WPS extract fails on a bad IBAN.

Contracts are fixed term, so an end date and a renewal cycle are mandatory data. Gratuity is computed on basic pay alone, so the package has to be split into basic, housing and transport on the contract. Ministerial Resolution 340 of 2026 moved payment to the first day of the following month with at least 85 percent transferred, so the WPS file cannot wait on late master data.

The statutory minimum is defined as components, QAR 1,000 basic plus QAR 500 accommodation and QAR 300 food unless the employer provides them directly, so one wage figure on the contract is not enough. QID expiry governs work eligibility. There is no Qatar payroll localisation and no native Salary Information File export, so the WPS file is a bought module or a build against the bank layout.

Since 1 March 2024 end of service for expatriate workers accrues as a monthly contribution to the Social Insurance Organisation, 4.2 percent of wage for the first three years and 8.4 percent after. Service before that date remains the employer liability, so every employee needs a continuous service date and a split at that boundary. WPS 2.0 through the LMRA portal makes the payroll file the only permitted route.

Statutory identifiers carry the load: UAN and PF member ID, ESIC number where the wage threshold applies, PAN and Aadhaar. Professional tax is levied per state, so the work location on an employee is a tax input, not merely an address. Under the labour codes in force since November 2025, fixed term staff qualify for gratuity after one year, which turns contract type into a field that costs money.

There is no Odoo payroll localisation, so salary tax slabs, EOBI and provincial social security are built on the project and maintained at each budget. EOBI is calculated on the federal minimum wage rather than actual salary, which generic builds get wrong. Registration is with PESSI in Punjab or SESSI in Sindh, so the province of the work location has to sit on the employee record, not just the city.

Odoo ships no UK payroll localisation and the documented route is an integration with an external payroll product, so real time information submissions and auto enrolment assessment happen outside the HR record. What stays in Odoo is the data those systems need: national insurance number, address, starter declaration, and right to work evidence with its own expiry date for anyone holding a share code.

A system able to record working time is subject to co-determination, so the works council agrees the attendance and reporting design before go live rather than after it. The Nachweisgesetz requires the essential terms of employment in writing, so the contract record carries more than a wage and a date. There is no German payroll localisation, and the personal tab needs a documented purpose and retention rule.

faqs.q: Do we need Odoo Enterprise for HR?
faqs.a: Not for the directory. Employees, departments, job positions, the org chart, skills, contracts, onboarding plans, Time Off, Attendance, Timesheets and Recruitment are all Community. Payroll, Appraisals, Documents, Sign, Approvals and Planning are Enterprise. If a payslip has to be produced inside Odoo, that means Enterprise or a third party payroll module, and the third party route puts the maintenance on you.

faqs.q: Does every employee need a paid user licence?
faqs.a: No. Odoo charges for internal users who log in to the backend. People who are paid, appear on a roster or check in at a shared kiosk need no login. On most manufacturing, retail and construction projects the user count is a small fraction of headcount, so confirm who genuinely needs backend access before sizing the subscription.

faqs.q: Can Odoo track visa, iqama and Emirates ID expiry?
faqs.a: Yes. Work permit number, visa number and their expiry dates are native fields on the employee, and Odoo can raise a scheduled activity for the responsible HR user ahead of the date. What it does not give you out of the box is one renewals view across passports, permits, medical cards and certifications, so most GCC projects add a computed next expiry date and build a list on it.

faqs.q: Can Odoo calculate end of service gratuity?
faqs.a: Only through payroll, and only where a rule book exists for the country. Gratuity is a salary rule reading basic pay and continuous service, so it needs the package split into basic and allowances plus a joining date that predates the first Odoo contract. Where Odoo ships no localisation, the rule is written during the project and revisited whenever the law moves.

faqs.q: Can a line manager see salaries?
faqs.a: Not unless you place them in the HR Officer group, and that group is all or nothing across personal data. A manager outside any HR group sees the public employee record, work contact details, department and the requests of their own team. Restricting an Officer to a single department or company is a record rule written during implementation, not a setting somebody switches on.

faqs.q: What does migrating the old HR data actually involve?
faqs.a: Four files rather than one. Employees, then managers in a second pass, then contracts carrying the historical joining date, then opening leave balances as allocation records. Add document attachments if those are moving, which is usually the largest part by volume. The identifiers worth keeping are the legacy employee number and the bank account, because attendance hardware and the bank file both depend on them.

faqs.q: Can one database run several countries?
faqs.a: Yes, with one company per legal entity. An employee belongs to a company, so somebody working across two entities is two employee records linked to a single login. Working schedules, leave types, public holidays and salary structures are all set per company. What you get in return is one directory, one org chart and consolidated headcount reporting across the group.

faqs.q: Does Odoo HR work in Arabic?
faqs.a: Odoo ships Arabic with right to left support, and the interface language follows the user, so an Arabic speaking HR officer and an English speaking finance manager share one database. Field labels added during implementation need translating deliberately, and printed documents in Arabic need a font that renders correctly in the PDF engine, which is worth testing before go live rather than after.

faqs.q: How do we handle onboarding steps owned by other teams?
faqs.a: Put them in the plan and assign them to the owning role. One activity plan can create items for IT, finance and facilities against the same employee record, so HR sees a single checklist while each team sees only its own item in its own inbox. Steps that need a signed document or an approval sit in separate apps, and both of those are Enterprise.
